chunks: From him, from Muhammad ibn Isa ibn Abi Badr, from Ubayd ibn Zurarah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
A man is fasting, and he is asked, 'Are you fasting?' He says, 'No.' Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said, 'This is a lie.'
ai.seo_question: Is it considered lying if a fasting person says 'No' when asked if they are fasting?
ai.summary: In the chapter on 'Additions' (al-Ziyadat), Imam al-Sadiq clarifies that concealing one's fast to avoid ostentation (riya') or modesty (takhalluf) constitutes a lie, as the reality of the fast remains unchanged. This highlights the Shia scholarly emphasis on truthfulness in worship, distinguishing between hidden sincerity and deceptive concealment. The ruling underscores that the act of fasting is a factual state, and denying it verbally invalidates the truthfulness required in religious practice.
